proof_audit.assessment: Both directions finance every spot/deposit/forward leg and cover the foreign repayment. No-arbitrage forces K R_F=S0 R_H only under common maturity/credit, two-way executable trades, zero initial forward price and no omitted costs or restrictions. Finite reciprocal quote changes are 25% and -20%, not sign reversals.

Full margin needs u+x-m>=0. All positive receipts arrive before negative NDF then debt; u+x-m+t+rho Gpositive-Gnegative-D>=0 therefore also funds every intermediate payment. The maximum with zero is necessary and sufficient because the contribution adds no repayment or altered flows. Actual insufficient-funding journals retain nonnegative cash and outstanding claims; the translated conservation identity includes late assets without treating them as early cash.

The five original affine constraints follow from dated cash. Weights 30/47 on squeeze early and 17/47 on weak late cancel h and give lower bound 48/47. Hedge 2720/47 attains it, other requirements -428/47, -204/47 and zero lie below; residual notional is 1040/47. General candidate completeness follows from affine-order intervals on the compact domain. Separate interval elimination verifies the global minimum and leftmost tie in eight bounded designs without copying that search.

H service is paid first, only remaining H buys actual F, and F imports precede debt above the usable floor. Adding required uses proves the minimum extra timely F receipt, conditional on earlier H payment and unchanged purchase behavior. Closing principal is named arrears plus old future debt plus actual new principal. Expanding translated opening/closing stocks proves the revaluation/transaction bridge; it is not a cash source.

The action is eligible only if F capacity covers the full promise. Given eligibility, the repayment-score advantage is C-SD; the tie rule is explicit. The model does not infer preferences from capacity or predict a sovereign equilibrium. Date-specific positive discount factors value the separate creditor claims, without pricing default risk or proving future repayment.
